method: exact integer-cell placement and complement enumeration
computed_answer_actual_content: Outline E cannot be formed without flipping a piece.
continuous_rotation_completeness_proof: Take any convex 90-degree corner of the target. Every tile corner is 90 or 270 degrees, so exactly one tile occupies a neighborhood of that corner. Its corner coincides with the target corner, with both incident edges aligned to the target edges. Its rotation is therefore a multiple of 90 degrees, and its translation maps an integer vertex to an integer vertex. After removing this first tile, every boundary segment and vertex of the remaining tile comes from the target or the first tile. They lie on the same integer orthogonal lattice, forcing the second tile also to have a quarter-turn rotation and integer translation. Thus the finite exact cell enumeration covers every permitted continuous rotation/translation.
